finding.claim: Missing authorization on /admin/drop: the Authorize() error is discarded, so any authenticated user can run the DROP TABLE path regardless of role.
finding.source: HTTP route /admin/drop registered at api.go:44, handled by dropTable (api.go:24) with user from request context (api.go:25)

trace.note: user loaded from request context via userFrom
runSQL executes DROP TABLE regardless of authorization result
Authorize returns errors.New("forbidden") for non-DBA users, so the check is effective but unused

finding.guards_checked: Authorize role check (api.go:13-20) exists but its error is not checked at api.go:26. Sibling vacuum handler (api.go:33-35) checks the error and returns 403, so this omission is specific to dropTable. No auth middleware in this repo sets the user context value; enforcement of route-level authentication is UNCERTAIN.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize role check at api.go:13-20 exists, but its error is discarded by the bare call at api.go:26, so it has no effect. The sibling vacuum handler at api.go:33-35 checks the error correctly, which confirms the omission is specific to dropTable. No other guard is in the repo. The only remaining control is upstream authentication, which sets the context user and is not in this repo.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: /admin/drop is routed to dropTable at api.go:44, and the Authorize result is discarded at api.go:26, so runSQL("DROP TABLE " + ...) at api.go:27 runs for any user whose context is set, whatever their roles. Caveat: the authentication that populates the context at api.go:22 is outside this repo, so the reachable attacker is any authenticated user, not anonymous. Without a valid user in context, userFrom panics on the type assertion, which is a crash rather than an exploit.

finding.claim: SQL injection: the form value t is concatenated directly into a DROP TABLE statement with no allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameter binding.
finding.source: r.FormValue("t") at api.go:27 (query string or form body; method not restricted)
finding.sink: runSQL("DROP TABLE " + t) at api.go:27, runSQL stub at api.go:41

trace.note: r.FormValue("t") read and concatenated into SQL string
runSQL receives the string; body is an empty stub in this file, so real behavior is not visible

finding.guards_checked: No validation, allowlist, quoting, or parameterized query on the value at api.go:27. Reaching the sink requires passing the route, which is subject to finding F1 and to unseen route-level authentication (UNCERTAIN). Severity depends on the production runSQL implementation, e.g. whether it allows multiple statements.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u, "dba") at api.go:26 is called as a bare statement, so its error return is discarded and it does not block the request. No allowlist, identifier quoting, or parameter binding is applied to t at api.go:27. The route at api.go:44 is registered directly with no wrapping middleware in this file. The vacuum handler at api.go:33-36 shows the correct pattern, which dropTable does not follow.
verdict.reason: The value at api.go:27 is concatenated into "DROP TABLE " + r.FormValue("t") with no protection, and the only role check at api.go:26 discards Authorize's error, so any caller that gets past the unseen user-context middleware (which userFrom at api.go:22 assumes exists) reaches the sink. Caveats: runSQL at api.go:41 is an empty stub, so actual impact (for example multi-statement execution) cannot be confirmed from this file, and the upstream middleware that sets the "user" context value is not visible.
